column7: fourth #2700 site: markWebAuthnCredentialClonedDisabled (the disable-on-clone-signal mutation) persisted through a bare Save, and WebAuthnCredential is HARD-deleted, so a passkey the user removed inside the window was re-INSERTED. It comes back with Disabled=true so it FAILS CLOSED for authentication -- the damage is to the credential count and the webauthn_enabled bookkeeping derived from it, not access. Low severity, stated as such. Fixed by DisableWebAuthnCredential (disabled alone, RowsAffected-checked, deliberately unconditional on the current value since disabling is monotone); AdvanceWebAuthnCredentialCounter's sibling Save -- which #2700 classes SAFE because it holds SELECT ... FOR UPDATE in the same transaction -- moved to SetWebAuthnCredentialCounterState too, so the model has no full-row writer left at all. Red on real Postgres: the credential row existed again after a delete that reported success
